stories.headline: Putin vows retaliation after Ukraine hits Russian oil plants
body: Putin says Ukraine keeps attacking Russian oil refineries despite Trump asking it to stop.
He called retaliation 'inevitable'.
Kyiv says it will stop hitting Russian energy sites only when Moscow does the same.
stories.vc: Refinery strikes can push up fuel prices across Europe and beyond.

stories.headline: Colombia's president blames ex-FARC rebels for a car bomb
body: A car bomb hit a state government building in Villavicencio, injuring at least 23 people.
President Abelardo de la Espriella blamed a commander of the ex-FARC group EMC.
He says the attack was revenge for government offensives and vowed to retaliate.
stories.vc: Rising violence can scare off investment in Colombia's regions.

stories.headline: Houthi drone hits a tower in Riyadh's financial district
body: A Houthi drone attack on a tower in Riyadh's financial district injured at least 11 people.
They include two Indians, three Nepalis, four Egyptians and two Saudis.
The Houthis have been firing at Saudi targets since Yemen's war reignited in July.
stories.vc: Attacks on business districts raise risk for Gulf investment and expat workers.

stories.headline: India's AI funding nearly doubles to $1.6 billion
body: Indian AI companies raised $1.6 billion in the first nine months of 2026, up 96%, says Tracxn.
Mumbai overtook Bengaluru as the top city for AI funding.
Deals fell from 149 to 87, but average deal size more than tripled to $18.5 million.
stories.vc: Money is concentrating in a few big AI bets like Neysa and Sarvam.

stories.headline: SEBI asks market players to stop publishing IPO 'grey market' prices
body: SEBI told brokers and other registered players to stop publishing grey market premium (GMP) figures for upcoming IPOs.
GMP is an unofficial price at which shares change hands before listing.
SEBI says these deals are unregulated and offer investors no protection.
stories.joke: The grey market just got greyer.
stories.vc: Fewer hype numbers could cool speculative IPO frenzies.

stories.headline: SpiceJet shrinks to six planes and about 20 flights a day
body: Embattled SpiceJet now flies just six aircraft and a little over 20 flights a day, sources say.
DGCA sent the airline a show-cause notice over cancellations and delayed payments.
Complaints against it rose to 8,671 on the government's AirSewa dashboard.
stories.joke: Fleet size: one cricket team, minus five.
stories.vc: Fewer seats can push up fares on busy domestic routes.

stories.headline: Unhedged asks if Huang's return is a bad day for capitalism
body: FT's Unhedged podcast says Jensen Huang is back as Nvidia CEO after 11 days out.
Nvidia's shares fell sharply while he was gone.
Hosts Katie Martin and Rob Armstrong worry Trump's role makes it a dark day for US capitalism.
stories.joke: Board meeting, now with a presidential phone line.
stories.vc: Political influence over company boards adds a new risk for investors.

stories.headline: Anthropic shares fall below their IPO price
body: Anthropic's stock dropped as low as $76 on Tuesday, below its $83 IPO price.
It debuted on Nasdaq less than a week ago at $111.50.
Nvidia also fell more than 7%. (Axios Pro Rata had nothing checkable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.joke: From IPO pop to IPO flop in a week.
stories.vc: A weak debut could pressure private AI startup valuations and other AI IPOs.

stories.headline: Stratechery: Huang got 'the individual exception', and won't be the last
body: Ben Thompson says Jensen Huang was granted an exception from normal oversight.
He argues AI lets single individuals do work that once took whole teams.
In 1959 AT&T had 729,000 employees; Nvidia's market value per employee is now about $95 million.
stories.vc: Tiny teams with huge valuations change how investors judge companies.

stories.headline: Amazon buys Decart to narrow the AI-chip gap with Nvidia
body: Amazon is acquiring Decart's tech and team for a reported $7.5 billion.
Decart helps AI models run well on non-Nvidia chips, like Amazon's Trainium.
Anthropic and Nvidia were also reportedly interested.
stories.joke: Can't beat the chips? Buy the software.
stories.vc: Better software for rival chips could weaken Nvidia's pricing power.

image.credit: Ajay Suresh from New York, NY, USA / Wikimedia Commons

stories.headline: Electric truck maker Harbinger raises over $100M, including from Palmer Luckey's bank
body: Harbinger secured more than $100 million, including debt from Palmer Luckey's Erebor Bank.
It comes less than three weeks after a $240 million Series D round.
FedEx has ordered 2,000 of its trucks. (No Economist piece was readable, so this is TechCrunch's report.)
stories.vc: Debt alongside equity lets startups grow without giving away as much ownership.

stories.statLabel: women killed by partners or family
stories.headline: UN: five women an hour were killed by a partner or relative last year
body: About 47,000 women and girls were killed by a partner or family member in 2025, the UN says.
That is five every hour, or 129 a day.
The report says home remains the most dangerous place for women and girls.
stories.vc: Violence costs women their lives and economies their workers and leaders.

stories.headline: Another US congressman resigns over sexual misconduct
body: Democrat Jimmy Gomez says he will resign on December 1.
A House Ethics Committee report found evidence he 'engaged in sexual misconduct' toward a staffer.
He is one of about six House members to face such allegations this year.
stories.vc: Safer workplaces help women build careers in politics.

stories.statLabel: law that covers arrests of women
stories.headline: Delhi Police tells Supreme Court women protesters needn't be handled only by women officers
body: Women protesters and journalists say male officers manhandled them at recent Delhi protests.
Delhi Police told the Supreme Court the women-officer rule covers arrests and searches, not crowd control.
Petitions came from the Network of Women in Media and journalist groups.
stories.vc: Clear rules protect women's right to protest and report safely.

stories.headline: Trichy government hospital gets a new 600-bed building
body: CM Joseph Vijay was set to open a 600-bed super speciality building at Trichy's MGM Government Hospital on November 20.
It has a ground floor plus six floors over about 2.1 lakh sq ft.
Patients come from Karur, Perambalur, Ariyalur and Pudukkottai too.
stories.vc: Bigger public hospitals ease crowding and cut waits for poorer patients.

stories.headline: Max Healthcare plans to add over 8,900 beds
body: Max Healthcare outlined plans to add more than 8,900 beds, about 4,600 in the next three to four years.
It set aside ₹7,362 crore of capital spending.
First-half network revenue rose 18% to ₹6,200 crore.
stories.joke: Beds: Max's favourite unit of growth.
stories.vc: Private chains are betting heavily on rising demand for hospital care.

stories.headline: Aster to open a 300-bed hospital in Hyderabad
body: Aster DM Quality Care will open a 300-bed hospital at Kondapur, Hyderabad, in March 2027.
It costs ₹500 crore and includes 100 critical care beds and 10 operating theatres.
Aster's Hyderabad capacity will pass 1,700 beds.
stories.joke: Kondapur's newest tower: this one heals.
stories.vc: More critical-care beds help a fast-growing city handle emergencies.

stories.headline: Avelacom opens the fastest fibre route between ASX and CME
body: Avelacom built a new fibre route between ASX's Sydney data centre and CME's Aurora, Illinois data centre.
It says the round trip takes 170.85 milliseconds, the fastest fibre path available.
It targets firms running arbitrage and cross-market strategies.
stories.joke: Australia to Chicago faster than you can blink twice.
stories.vc: Faster links help prices stay in line between markets.

stories.headline: LMAX brings institutional perpetual futures to brokers via Helio
body: LMAX Group launched institutional perpetual futures on Fintake's Helio trading platform.
Brokers can offer them alongside FX and CFDs from a single account.
Brokers with LMAX access can go live in under five days.
stories.joke: Futures that never expire, set up in days.
stories.vc: Easier access could pull more crypto trading onto regulated venues.

stories.statLabel: about a fifth of a second
stories.headline: Explainer: Why do traders care about speed?
body: Imagine two kids racing to the school shop when new sweets arrive. The first one there gets the best pick.
Traders call the travel time of a message 'latency'. Less latency means you arrive first.
This week, Avelacom opened the fastest fibre route between Sydney's stock exchange and a big US exchange in Illinois.
A message goes there and back in about 171 milliseconds, less than a fifth of a second.
Firms trading in both places use it so their orders land before prices change.
stories.vc: Speed shapes who profits.

stories.headline: Cadillac keeps Bottas for 2027, leaving Colton Herta as reserve
body: Cadillac will keep Valtteri Bottas alongside Sergio Perez in 2027.
American Colton Herta left IndyCar and earned the 40 superlicence points needed for F1.
He is now set to be reserve driver, and faces a big career decision.
stories.joke: Did all the homework, still didn't get the seat.
stories.vc: An American driver would help Cadillac's sponsor and TV appeal in the US.
